title: Screen Ambience
subtitle: The LEDs copy your monitor's colors and can follow the mood of your PC's music.
missing: Screen Ambience wasn't found in this installation.
offNote: Off — turn it on so the LEDs follow the screen
explain: What you see above is what the LEDs are seeing: each light copies the area of the screen at the same spot where you placed the device in Lighting → Layout. The screen image is never recorded or sent anywhere.
noAudio: Windows didn't share the PC audio — only the image is working.
nativeStopped: Native capture stopped ({error}); using Chromium capture.
nativeUnavailable: Native capture unavailable ({error}); using Chromium capture.
waitingMusic: Waiting for music… (no PC audio right now)
explainMixer: Each column is the volume of one band of the music, from bass (left) to treble (right), in the colors of the mood going to the LEDs. The light line on top is each band's recent peak.
reactSoundOnly: With "PC sound" the lights follow only the music: screen colors are left out (neutral background) and, with no music, the LEDs go dark.
calibHelp: If the app usually reads your music as sadder or more aggressive than you feel it, nudge it here. The automatic analysis still applies; this only shifts the result.
toneNow: Colors going to the LEDs now
keyHint: Key of the music playing now, estimated from the chords. A minor key pulls the colors toward sad; a major key, toward happy.
